title: Rami bar Berabbi or Berukhi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Sanhedrin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.17b.6) they said (wherever it says “the Neharbelaim teach”) that it is Rami bar Berabbi; Hyman reports the form Rami bar Berukhi from the Arukh, entry נהר, Rashi on Beitzah 8b, and Dikdukei Soferim. And what is cited in Seder HaDorot, “bar Beruni” — the author of Maskil LeEitan writes that bar Beruni is not found anywhere; Hyman objects that he overlooked a small error in Seder HaDorot, proposing “bar Berukhi,” and explaining that the kaf was slightly erased, leaving a nun. Yuchasin cites bar Berekhyah.[^2][^1]
In Sefer HaKeritot, Leshon Limmudim, gate 3, he wrote: “The Neharbelaim teach” — this is Rav Bivi bar Bizna.

notes.text: The consulted [Rashi on Beitzah](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Beitzah.8b.10.1) refers the reader to the Sanhedrin identification and reads bar Beribi. [Heilprin’s first Neharbelai entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2610&lang=en) records bar Berivi and bar Rivyoni alongside the Arukh’s bar Berukhi. His [second entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2611&lang=en) gives Rav Bivi bar Bizna. The proposed damaged letter and the Yuchasin reading remain Hyman’s account.

The consulted [Arukh, Nehar Balai](https://torahwords.org/aru_1504#a4768) gives Rami bar Berukhi. The commentary printed with the entry contrasts bar Berukhi with bar Berabbi in its current text. The linked Rashi gives bar Beribi.
